rules.title: Eviction ground: permanent removal of property from rental market for redevelopment/blight clearance (relocation assistance)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict where a governmental agency wants to permanently take the property off the rental market for redevelopment or clearing blighted land. Three months' Notice to Quit is required and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Law (coverage rules stated elsewhere in the document).
rules.quoted_span: The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.ambiguity_note: Chunk begins mid-section; the opening of the ground is in the prior chunk.

rules.title: Eviction ground: permanently retiring property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord permanently retiring a building or mobile home park from residential use may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing; no action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: refusal of reasonable lease changes
rules.requirement: At lease expiration a landlord may propose reasonable but substantial lease changes; if the tenant refuses after written notice, the landlord may sue and the court decides reasonableness. One month's Notice to Quit is required.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law; landlord bears burden of proof for protected tenancies.
rules.quoted_span: If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable.

rules.title: Eviction ground: continuous non-payment or habitual late payment of rent
rules.requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a landlord may sue to evict a tenant who continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late. One month's Notice to Quit is required.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple
rules.requirement: A landlord converting property to condo, co-op or fee simple of two or more units may sue for eviction after a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing, with stays of eviction available and protection for senior/disabled protected tenants.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or sites.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must comply with the regulations governing conversion to condominiums and cooperatives, before a warrant for possession shall be issued.
rules.key_value: 3 years' Notice to Quit; up to five one-year stays

rules.title: Eviction ground: sale to owner-occupant after conversion (tenancy began after master deed)
rules.requirement: Owner of a building being converted may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded if the unit is sold to a buyer who will personally occupy it and the contract calls for vacancy; tenant must have been given a conversion statement; two months' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, cooperative agreement or subdivision plat was recorded.
rules.quoted_span: However, no action shall be brought against a tenant under paragraph one (1) of this subsection unless the tenant was given a statement, informing the tenant that the property is being converted.

rules.title: Eviction ground: owner of three or fewer condo/co-op units seeking personal occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: Owner of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units may evict a tenant whose rental began after the master deed was recorded if the owner will personally occupy or has contracted to sell to a buyer who will occupy; two months' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of three or less condominium or cooperative units seeks to evict a tenant whose initial tenancy began, by rental, after the master deed or agreement establishing the cooperative was recorded, because the owner seeks to personally occupy the unit, or has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Eviction ground: owner of building with three or fewer units seeking personal occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: Owner of a building with three residential units or less may evict to personally occupy a unit or to deliver it vacant to a buyer who will occupy it; two months' Notice to Quit and no action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building with three residential units or less seeks to personally occupy a unit, or has contracted to sell the residential unit to a buyer who wishes to personally occupy it and the contract fo r sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Eviction ground: termination of employment-based tenancy
rules.requirement: Where a tenant lives in the property on condition of employment by the landlord and the employment is terminated, the landlord may sue for eviction after a three-day Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing in the property as a condition of employment.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: drug offense conviction on the property
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of or pleading guilty to drug offenses on the property (unless in rehabilitation), or who lets such a person occupy the premises; suit must be brought within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Eviction ground: conviction for assault or terrorist threats against landlord, family or employees
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employees, or who permits such a person to reside there; suit within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found by the court to be delinquent due to an offense involving assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landl ord’s family or an employee of the landlord.

rules.title: Eviction ground: civil court finding of liability for theft, assault or drug activity
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant found liable in a civil proceeding for theft on the premises, assault or terrorist threats against the landlord's side, or illegal drug activity on the premises; suit within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant is found by a civil court proceeding (not criminal) to be liable fo r involvement in theft of property located on the premises

rules.title: Eviction ground: conviction for theft of property
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of theft from the landlord or other tenants in the building, or who permits such a person to reside there; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found to be delinquent by the Court due to an offense involving theft of property from the landlord or from tenants residing in the same building or complex.

rules.title: Eviction ground: human trafficking violation
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant found in a civil action to have committed human trafficking violations on the premises or to have harbored a person engaged in human trafficking; action must be brought within two years after the violation ends.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: No action for removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought mor e than two years after the alleged violation has terminated (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(r)).

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings may be removed only by court order, and the landlord must prove one of the listed causes (holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, willful damage, constant rule violations, lease violation with re-entry right). Notice-to-quit periods vary by cause and tenancy type.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.key_value: 3-day, 1-month or 3-month notice to quit depending on cause/tenancy

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions follow Eviction Law good cause
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and give three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction.

exemption_tests.description: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled are excepted from rooming/boarding house definition.

rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).
rules.key_value: 3 working days' notice to County Welfare Board

rules.title: Penalty: landlord must occupy unit six months after personal-occupancy eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord who gets a unit vacated by giving notice of personal occupancy must occupy it for at least six months; otherwise liable to the former tenant for three times damages plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants vacating after notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.
rules.penalty: Three times damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs

rules.title: Penalty: five-year bar on residential use after removal/retirement notice
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice of permanent board-up, demolition or retirement from residential use, the property may not be used residentially for five years; violations bring treble damages, fees and a civil penalty.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants vacating after notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.
rules.key_value: 5 years; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 per violation

rules.title: Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction; 90-day notice to quit for owner-occupant buyer
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction; a buyer of a foreclosed property who wants to occupy it as a primary residence must give a 90-day notice to quit and wait until any lease expires. Month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units are not exempt.
rules.quoted_span: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.
